content.intro: {state} charges {stateRate} sales and use tax on the price of a vehicle when it is titled, plus a title fee and a registration fee that depends on the vehicle's weight.

howItWorks.text: The tax rate is {stateRate} of the gross sales price. A trade-in does not lower the price the tax is figured on, and the state sets a minimum tax.
Registration is charged by weight class for passenger vehicles. Some Northern Virginia localities add an emissions inspection charge, and some localities add a local registration fee.
Vehicles with good fuel economy, and electric vehicles, can also owe a highway use fee set by a state formula. It is not included in the total.

faq.q: Does a trade-in lower the sales tax in Virginia?
faq.text: No. The state taxes the gross sales price after rebates and incentives. A trade-in, an unpaid lien or other credits do not reduce it.

faq.q: Is there a minimum sales and use tax?
faq.text: Yes. The state charges the greater of the percentage tax or a flat minimum amount.

faq.q: What is the highway use fee?
faq.text: It is a yearly fee on vehicles with good fuel economy, worked out from a state formula. It is not part of the total shown here.
